pillar_reactions.evidence: Rep delivered the 3-4x/week 30-40 minute structure plus 5-15 minute daily mobility and the 'teach you how to fish' framing. Prospect confirmed only: "Yes, it does" to "Does that all make sense to you?" No questions, no elaboration, no tie-back to his own goal.

The one pillar he volunteered energy on. On fasting: "I did actually see his post recently about the full moon cycle that he does once a month, and yeah, I really love that... I know how powerful it is, and not many people I know do it." He had named fasting and gut health as personal interests unprompted at 00:01:43.

On the app, video submissions, Trevor's personal chat and the nudging: "Transparency, yeah, for sure." And after the Thursday live workout / community add-on: "No, you've covered it pretty well, yeah, I'm on board with what you guys have to offer, I guess it just comes down to the payment systems." Understood and agreed, but moved straight to price.

anchors.raw: I was thinking like 200 bucks a month was something that I was willing to sacrifice... I typed into Google what it might cost to go down this endeavor and that's where I got the 200-a-month answer.
anchors.note: The anchor was set by a Google search two days before the call, not by a competitor he had used. He arrived expecting an app with video clips and occasional lives — a $200/mo subscription shape — and priced the entire category at that. A 30x gap the rep did not attempt to reframe; he matched the anchor instead.

anchors.raw: my partner is actually a personal trainer... she's got an app, and she can make me a weekly [plan]
anchors.competitor: Prospect's own partner (qualified personal trainer, free)
anchors.note: He has free, qualified programming at home and already uses it. His stated reason for looking elsewhere is modality (kettlebells) and his partner's bias toward weights training — not absence of coaching. Nobody differentiated the paid offer against the free one in the house.

anchors.raw: Save his routines that he posts on Facebook and write them down and implement them myself, but it's just very time-consuming copying and pasting his work
anchors.note: The prospect is already consuming the coach's free output and getting some of the value. His stated complaint is transcription effort and not knowing if his form is right — a narrow, cheap-to-solve problem, which makes the $200/mo tier feel proportionate to him and the $6,000 tier feel absurd.

anchors.raw: currently trying to buy a house. Currently, the single income owner of the house we're in, we're renting... I'm going to Brisbane to go to a business conference for my partner
anchors.note: Household is running a house deposit, a partner's business launch and a conference on one income. The $6,000 competes against capital allocation, not against other coaching.

unmet_demand.want: A self-paced kettlebell education — understanding the why behind the movements well enough to eventually coach others alongside his partner
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is delivered as one-to-one transformation coaching toward a personal goal. Certification, teaching methodology or coach-track content was never mentioned, though the rep did lean on the 'teach you how to fish' framing.

unmet_demand.want: Form correction while training away from home in a hotel room with no equipment
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The tier he was actually sold (Primal Instinct University) is community-based with group correction, not the one-to-one video review the rep described in the $6,000 presentation. His specific need — knowing whether he is doing the movements correctly — is the thing the cheaper tier serves least well.
